The study states that DHIS2 is implemented nationwide, including all CSPS facilities, the first level of a three-tier public system, as monthly reports keyed by the district; in its two districts report completeness was 100% (34 facilities, Toma) and 95.5% to 100% (36 facilities, Gourcy) over December 2017 to December 2021. The Countdown to 2030 country team reports that the share of expected monthly facility reports in DHIS2 fell from 93% in 2020 to 83% in 2024 (94, 89 and 89 in between), and the share of districts with report completeness of 90% or more fell from 78% to 50%, which it attributes to facility closures and population displacement from insecurity.

The Pan African Medical Journal study states that an electronic HMIS on DHIS2 was introduced in 2013 and that monthly activity reports of health facilities, in its two districts 60 primary health care centres and 2 medical centres, reach the central warehouse EnDoS/DHIS2 through the districts; across 15 health districts completeness was above 91% in all but one in 2016 and 2018 and fell to between 49% and 97.5% in 2019. It says the performance of regional and university hospitals is not measured separately.

The study reports, for 2016 to 2019, that monthly activity reports are transmitted from each health district to the central level, that data entry on EnDoS varies between districts of one region, and that the flow from the district information and surveillance centre (CISSE) into the system suffers from missing or late data entry.
